subject: Engelska
title: Vocabulary: everyday words and phrasal verbs
sourceSummary: Common phrasal verbs and words that are often mixed up — the foundation for sounding natural in everyday spoken and written English.

questions.prompt: What does "turn off" mean in: "Please turn off the lights before you leave."
questions.opener: What do you do to a lamp when you leave the room?
choices: Switch something so it stops working
questions.explanation: "Turn off" means to switch something off (e.g. a device or a light). The opposite is "turn on".

questions.prompt: Choose the phrasal verb that fits: "Can you ___ the volume? I can't hear the movie."
questions.opener: Which expression means to increase something?
questions.explanation: "Turn up" means to increase (e.g. volume). "Turn down" is the opposite — to lower it.

questions.prompt: What does "give up" mean in: "Don't give up, you're almost finished!"
questions.opener: What should you NOT do when you're almost done?
questions.explanation: "Give up" means to stop trying, to quit. Saying "don't give up" is encouragement to keep going.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrasal verb that fits: "I need to ___ what "ubiquitous" means."
questions.opener: What do you do when you don't know what a word means — you look it up.
questions.explanation: "Look up" means to look something up, e.g. in a dictionary or online. "Look for" means to search for, "look after" means to take care of.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes: "I'm really ___ about the test tomorrow. I haven't studied enough."
questions.opener: Which word describes a worried feeling about something that's about to happen?
questions.explanation: "Nervous" fits the feeling before a test you haven't finished studying for. "Boring" describes something dull and doesn't describe a feeling you have yourself.

questions.opener: Who FEELS bored, and what IS boring?
choices: I was boring during the movie.
I was bored during the movie.
questions.explanation: "Bored" describes how a person feels. "Boring" describes what causes that feeling. A movie can be "boring", but only a person can be "bored".

questions.prompt: Fill in the correct phrasal verb for each blank, choosing from: turn off, look after, give up, turn up. "Could you (1) ___ my dog while I'm away? Also, remember to (2) ___ the heater before you leave. And please don't (3) ___ on your homework — the last question just needs you to (4) ___ the answer in a dictionary."
questions.opener: Four different phrasal verbs, four different meanings: take care of, switch off, quit, look something up.
questions.answer: 1) look after (take care of), 2) turn off (switch off), 3) give up (quit), 4) look up (look something up).
steps: "___ my dog" means to take care of the dog — that matches "look after", not "look up" or "turn up" (increase/show up).
"___ the heater" before leaving the room means to switch it off — "turn off".
"don't ___ on your homework" means don't quit — "give up".
"___ the answer in a dictionary" means to look up the answer — "look up".

questions.prompt: List common everyday phrasal verbs and what they mean.
questions.opener: Eight common phrasal verbs to know by heart.
questions.answer: turn on/off = to switch on/off · turn up/down = to increase/decrease (volume) · look up = to look something up (e.g. in a dictionary) · look after = to take care of · look for = to search for · give up = to quit/stop trying · find out = to discover · get up = to get out of bed · pick up = to collect/fetch · put on = to dress in (clothes).
